To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photon index of the power-law spectral component is correlated with the position along the branches on the HID of the peculiar low mass X-ray binary Circin X-1, which is consistent with the scenario in which the power-law spectral hard component is produced by inverse Compton scattering of the soft photons by relativistic electrons.
we find that the power-law component is correlated with the hardness-intensity diagram position and dominates the high-energy band of the X-ray spectrum.
we detect a power-law component in the spectra of Cir X- 1, which is correlated with the position of the source on the HID, and the power-law component dominates in the energy band above ~20 keV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hard X-ray emission from Cir X-1.
the hard X-ray spectra of the peculiar X-ray binary Cir X-1 along its branches in its HID.
the evolution of the X-ray spectra in Cir X-1 along its branches on the HID.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power-law hard X-ray component is a result of Compton scattering of soft photons in the accretion disk by a population of energetic electrons in the accretor.
the power-law component in the spectra of Cir X- 1 is most likely a result of Comptonization.
the hard component in the X-ray spectra of Cir X- 1 is most likely the result of Comptonization of thermal electrons by soft photons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of the spectra along the branches on the HID is mainly caused by the change of the spectral properties of the hard component.
the power-law hard components in the spectra of Cir X- 1 are likely due to inverse Compton scattering of soft photons by hot electrons in the accretion disk or corona.

the power-law hard components are likely to be related with the accretion process of the system, which may be caused by the interaction between the stellar wind of the companion star and the accretion flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power-law hard X-ray component in the spectra of Cir X- 1 is a persistent one.
we have detected a hard X-ray power law that is correlated with the source position on the hardness-intensity diagram.

the power-law hard spectral component dominates the hard X-ray emission of the low-mass X-Ray binary Cir X-1, and its flux is correlated with the position of Cir X-0 on the hardness-intensity diagram.
